newsitem.title: USA: Conrail says boosts on-time performance.
newsitem.headline: Conrail says boosts on-time performance.

text.p: LAKE BUENA VISTA, Florida, Jan 30, Reuter - Some nine of every 10 freight shipments carried by Conrail, one of the biggest railroads in the U.S., arrived at their destination on time in 1996, a company executive said on Thursday.
"We were able to achieve over 90% performance for most of the year," said Timothy Dwyer, senior vice president in charge of Conrail's unit train service group.

The 1996 on-time performance record matched that of the previous year, even though the company had substantially narrowed the window in which a train's arrival would be considered "on time", Dwyer said in a speech before the National Mining Association's annual transportation conference here.

Trains were considered late when they did not arrive one hour before or after the scheduled delivery time. In past years, a train was considered late only if it arrived more than 24 hours outside of the promised delivery time.
In 1997, Conrail has raised its on-time performance goal to 95 percent, he said.

In addition, the company plans to cut in half the average amount of time an empty unit train remains at the customer after it has been unloaded. "Empty-dwell" times should average about six hours following a train's release by customers, he said.
Conrail, the dominant freight railroad in the northeastern U.S., is currently the object of a fierce takeover battle between CSX Corp and Norfolk Southern Corp.
